title: IPscore NPV Target Planner — EPO · ASP Adaptation
brand: IPscore NPV Target Planner — EPO Tool • ASP Adaptation
sub: Work backwards from your target: find what it takes to reach your NPV goal

page0.title: 🎯 Set Your Target
page0.desc: Tell us about your company and the NPV you want to achieve. We will guide you through the key factors and show you in real time whether your situation can reach the goal.
page0.bt_hint: (entire company, not just the patent area)
page0.tpct_note: Typical range: 5–25% of turnover. The higher the target, the more demanding the required patent parameters.
page0.sector_note: What share of your total revenues comes from the market segment where this patent operates?
page0.costs_note: All running costs (production + overheads) as a percentage of your total turnover. Typical range: 65–85%.
page0.discount_note: Not sure? Use 10% as a safe default. Higher-risk businesses should use 12–15%.

page1.title: ⏰ Technology Window
page1.desc: This is the single most powerful parameter in the entire model. Answer honestly — the rest of the planning depends on it.
page1.why_box: 💡 Why does this matter so much? The NPV formula adds up cash flows over 10 years, discounting each one back to today. Every year of delay does two things simultaneously: it adds development costs in early years (negative) and delays when positive revenue starts (negative). These two effects compound, making time-to-market the dominant lever in almost every scenario.

page2.title: 🌎 Market Potential
page2.desc: Three questions that define how much revenue your patent can actually generate over its commercial life. Together, these are the primary source of positive value in the model.

page3.title: 📈 Financial Levers
page3.desc: Four questions about costs and investment. These determine how much of the market opportunity actually converts into net value after you account for what you must spend to achieve it.

page4.title: ⚖️ Legal & Strategic Foundation
page4.desc: The NPV you calculated in previous steps only materialises if the patent is well-protected and the company has a plan to exploit it. These six questions assess that foundation.
page4.note: ⓘ These questions do not change the NPV number — but they tell you how reliable that number is in practice.

page5.title: 🏆 Your Results
page5.desc: Here is a summary of where your patent stands relative to your NPV target — and what to prioritise.
page5.verdict_placeholder: Complete the previous steps to see your result.

results.bar_pct_template: You are at {pct}% of your target
results.verdict_no_data: Enter your company turnover and target on the Setup page to see your result.
results.verdict_reached: ✓ Target reached. Your current parameter profile supports an NPV that meets or exceeds your goal. Focus on defending this position — protect the technology, enforce the patent, and execute the commercial plan.
results.verdict_almost_template: ⚠ Almost there — {pct}% of target. You are close. One or two focused improvements in your weakest parameters should close the gap. See the priority actions below.
results.verdict_partway_template: ⚠ Partway there — {pct}% of target. Several parameters need strengthening. The NPV gap is real but closable. Prioritise the red-flagged items below.
results.verdict_gap_template: ❌ Significant gap — {pct}% of target. The current profile falls well short of the goal. Major changes in multiple parameters are required before the patent can justify its commercial target.
results.legal_rec_low: Work on patent grant status, remaining life, geographic coverage and claim breadth to build a solid legal foundation that can actually protect the NPV you are targeting.
results.legal_rec_mid: Legal position is adequate but has gaps. Prioritise the weakest legal element (coverage or enforceability) to reduce the risk of losing your competitive window unexpectedly.
results.legal_rec_high: Your legal foundation is solid. Keep monitoring for infringement and reassess coverage every 2–3 years.
results.strat_rec_low: A patent without a clear commercial plan rarely reaches its potential NPV. Define how you will use it: direct sales, licensing, or defensive positioning — and integrate it into your annual business plan.
results.strat_rec_mid: Your strategy is partially in place. Formalise the commercial plan and ensure leadership is committed to deploying the patent actively.
results.strat_rec_high: Excellent strategic alignment. Make sure the plan is reviewed annually and stays connected to business priorities.
results.actions_all_green: All key parameters are in the green zone. Maintain the current position, enforce the patent actively, and execute the commercial plan.
